content_voiceover: This is the flow chart for the TPOG-ALL-2021 protocol as revised for ETP and near ETP patients. Treatment begins with ETP induction, followed by an MRD check at MRD1, and induction continues regardless of that result. Then comes a second phase of ETP induction, followed by MRD2. After that, all patients move into venetoclax plus early intensification, the V-E-I phase, followed by MRD3. This MRD3 result is the key branch point. If MRD3 is less than 0.01 percent, the patient proceeds directly to high risk consolidation and then continuation therapy. If MRD3 is between 0.01 and 0.1 percent, the patient also goes to high risk consolidation, but then has an additional MRD check, MRD4, after that consolidation; if MRD4 is now less than 0.01 percent they proceed to continuation, but if it remains at or above 0.01 percent they move to treatment options. If MRD3 is 0.1 percent or higher, the patient goes straight to treatment options. Those treatment options include venetoclax combined with hyper-CVAD, nelarabine based therapy, or high dose ara-C based regimens such as reintensification regimen A. Patients who go down the treatment options pathway ultimately proceed to hematopoietic stem cell transplant. The footnote clarifies that MRD1 and MRD2 are used to judge the efficacy of ETP induction, while MRD3 is specifically obtained for ETP patients whose MRD2 was 0.01 percent or higher.
keypoints: Sequence: ETP induction, MRD1, ETP induction continued, MRD2, then V-E-I, then MRD3
MRD3 under 0.01 percent goes straight to consolidation and continuation
MRD3 between 0.01 and 0.1 percent needs an extra MRD4 check after consolidation
MRD3 at or above 0.1 percent, or a positive MRD4, leads to treatment options and eventual HSCT
Treatment options include venetoclax-hyper-CVAD, nelarabine-based therapy, or high-dose ara-C regimens
keypoint_voiceover: To summarize the flow. Patients go through ETP induction with MRD1, more induction with MRD2, then venetoclax plus early intensification leading to MRD3, which is the major decision point. MRD3 under 0.01 percent means straight to consolidation and continuation. Between 0.01 and 0.1 percent triggers an extra MRD4 check after consolidation. And MRD3 at 0.1 percent or higher, or a persistently positive MRD4, routes the patient to salvage treatment options like venetoclax hyper-CVAD, nelarabine, or high-dose ara-C, ultimately heading toward transplant.
